subject: Biotechnology
title: Farmer Rights and Seed Patents
description: Learn Farmer Rights and Seed Patents in one minute.

hook.text: Farmers saved seeds for 10,000 years — biotech patents made replanting your own harvest illegal.

buildup.text: Monsanto's technology agreements required farmers to buy new seed each year — replanting patented seeds meant a lawsuit.

discovery.text: Bowman v. Monsanto reached the Supreme Court — the farmer lost, affirming patent exhaustion does not cover self-replicating seeds.

twist.text: Terminator technology — seeds engineered to be sterile — was developed but never commercialized due to global outrage.

climax.text: Open-source seed initiatives release varieties without patent restrictions — the Open Source Seed Initiative guards seed freedom.

punchline.text: Who owns the seed owns the food supply — seed patents are biotech's hottest debate.

quiz.question: What did the Bowman v. Monsanto Supreme Court ruling establish?
options: Farmers have the right to save and replant any seeds they purchase
Patent exhaustion does not apply to self-replicating technologies like seeds, so replanting patented seeds is infringement
Monsanto must share its patented seeds with all farmers for free

details.summary: Biotechnology companies patent GM seeds and restrict farmers from saving and replanting harvested seed, requiring annual purchases. This practice raises concerns about corporate control of the food supply, farmer autonomy, and seed access in developing countries.
details.whyItMatters: Seed patents concentrate control of food genetics in a few corporations. Balancing incentives for biotech innovation with farmers' traditional right to save seed is a critical issue for food sovereignty and agricultural sustainability globally.
takeaways: GM seed patents prohibit farmers from saving and replanting purchased seed
A few corporations control the majority of commercial seed genetics globally
Developing countries face tensions between patent protection and food access

faq.question: Why can't farmers save and replant patented GM seeds?
faq.answer: Patent law grants seed companies exclusive rights to their inventions. Technology use agreements prohibit replanting because each harvest contains the patented genes. Companies argue patent protection funds the research needed to develop improved varieties.

faq.question: How do seed patents affect small farmers in developing countries?
faq.answer: Small farmers who traditionally save seed face increased costs from annual seed purchases. However, some programs provide GM seeds free or at subsidized rates. The balance between protecting innovation incentives and ensuring food access remains hotly debated.
